summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and a milestone-based timeline. Agreed to a 6-week POC with kickoff in early Jan, mid-point review, and exec readout. Security and access steps required before kickoff.
topics: Workload sizing (qps, sequence length, batch profiles)
Timeline & milestones (kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Maya che n from Redwood, and with me is Diego on the SE side.
[00:07] Diego (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. excited to kick off, we'll focus on the POC scope and milestone s today.
[00:15] Priya (Cascade ML): thanks — Priya here. we want to validate inference quality and unit cost for our transaction summarization workload, plus latency targets for realtime flows.
[00:24] Evan (Platform): Evan from platform. i'll own access and peering; we use GCP but plan to test both hosted and dedicated options.
[00:31] Liam (CTO): quick from me — priority is reliability and security, timeline is end of Q1 for production decision.
[00:38] Maya: great. high level we usually run a 4-6 week POC with clear milestones: kickoff, access setup, bench runs, mid-point review, and exec readout. that aligns?
[00:49] Priya: sounds right. What does success look like concretely?
[00:52] Diego: good question. we recommend a success criteria matrix — example rows: latency (p95 under X ms for a 256 token seq), throughput (qps meeting peak  requests), quality (ROUGE/F1 or custom metric on sample), and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:07] Priya: our current SLA target is p95 sub 200ms for short summaries (avg 120 tokens) and cost under $0.35 per 1k tokens ideally.
[01:16] Maya: ok that gives us targets. for workload sizing — Priya can you share qps distribution?
[01:21] Priya: yes, typical background is 2-3 qps per model instance, bursts to 20 qps during peak; average seq len 120 tokens, 99th around 500.
[01:31] Diego: good — we'll size the bench with a mix: baseline steady qps 3, ramp tests to 20, and long sequence runs to exercise KV cache and memory. Also we should test cold KV cache vs warm.
[01:45] Evan: for access, we need to know whether we do Redwood Hosted API or Redwood Dedicated in our VPC. we prefer Dedicated for data residency but will test hosted for a quick baseline.
[01:55] Maya: that makes sense — our recommended POC plan is: week 0 kickoff and access setup (hosted creds + optional VPC peering for dedicated), week 1 bench runs on hosted baseline, week 2-3 dedicated setup and full benchmark matrix, week 4 mid-point review, week 5 optimizations (batching, quant profiles), week 6 exec readout.
[02:10] Liam: six weeks workable, but can we compress? internal stakeholders want earlier readout.
[02:15] Maya: we can compress to 4 weeks by overlapping access setup and baseline runs, but tradeoff is less time for optimizations — Diego, thoughts?
[02:21] Diego: technically doable: run hosted benchmarks in parallel while infra team sets up VPC peering for Dedicated. must ensure we have sample data and runbooks ready to avoid delays.
[02:30] Priya: ok we'll prioritize providing data and a success criteria doc.
[02:33] Evan: i'll start the VPC peering request after receiving the CIDR.
[02:36] Diego: noted — we'll provide the network checklist and peering steps. (small pause) also, for benchmarks we'll measure: p50/p95 latency, tail latency spikes, throughput at target qps, token cost, and quality regressions on the sample set.
[02:51] Priya: for quality metrics we use a weighted F1 on entity extraction and a content-similarity score for summarization, we can provide the scoring script.
[02:59] Diego: perfect. on the runtime side we'll test model variants and quantization profiles — e.g., 8-bit quant vs full fp16 — to show cost/perf tradeoffs. please note some open model names might differ in our docs, we often reference Redwood-verified models and variants.
[03:15] Priya: any compliance blockers? we need SOC 2 plus encryption at rest and in transit; key management via our KMS preferred.
[03:23] Maya: yes, we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and offer customer-managed keys on Private. we'll send SOC 2 report and an ISO summary. Diego will attach SSO/SCIM and RBAC notes.
[03:34] Evan: also log retention and audit logs for queries — we need to ensure we can route logs to our SIEM.
[03:39] Diego: we have audit log export and can stream to GCS or PubSub; will include config examples.
[03:45] Liam: competition? any red flags vs Anthropic or OpenAI?
[03:47] Maya: customers sometimes compare unit cost and latency to hosted public APIs — Redwood differentiates with Dedicated performance and routing policies, plus transparent batching and caching. we'll show benchmark numbers.
[03:57] Priya: good. benchmark data share — what format do you want?
[04:00] Diego: CSV of sample inputs + gold labels, plus a small script that calculates the metrics, ideally a Dockerfile so we can reproduce scoring.
[04:08] Priya: we'll do that.
[04:10] Maya: ok let's talk milestone dates concretely. propose kickoff 2026-01-06, hosted baseline runs 1/6-1/9, dedicated infra 1/6-1/13, full benchmark 1/13-1/20, midpoint review 1/21, optimizations 1/22-1/28, exec readout 1/30. thoughts?
[04:29] Liam: those dates roughly align with our calendar. can we guarantee a midpoint demo with real numbers for execs? we need something compelling — e.g., cost delta and latency chart.
[04:38] Diego: yes, midpoint will include preliminary p95/p50 latencies, throughput, and a cost estimate per 1k tokens across profiles.
[04:45] Priya: can we include a run showing KV cache hit improvements? that's a big factor in our usage.
[04:50] Diego: absolutely — we'll include cold vs warm cache runs and show token/time per request.
[04:55] Evan: networking note — our security team requires a pen-test window and a short q/a with our InfoSec before peering. can Redwood provide details for that?
[05:03] Maya: yes we'll provide the security pack and a contact for InfoSec. Diego will be the technical point.
[05:08] Priya: about metrics — for cost comparisons please include host cost + Redwood overhead so we can compare apples-to-apples vs us running open models ourselves.
[05:16] Diego: we'll include a cost breakdown: GPU-hours, token cost, infra overhead, and optional dedicated pricing.
[05:22] Liam: one more question — will we be able to test model rollbacks and canary? we have a release guardrail requirement.
[05:28] Maya: yes — Redwood's rollout features support canary and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model on regressions. we'll demo in the ops console during the mid-point.
[05:36] Priya: ok next, documentation references — can you send the benchmark template and the SOW?
[05:40] Maya: will do. Diego: i'll attach the runbook and network checklist after this call.
[05:45] Evan: i'll wait on the CIDR and then open the peering ticket.
[05:48] Liam: sounds good. any other open risks?
[05:51] Priya: data privacy — some transaction notes are PII. we need to ensure tokens are not retained beyond the POC.
[05:57] Diego: we can set retention policies and show audit logs; Dedicated option supports no retention and customer managed keys. we'll document that.
[06:05] Maya: to recap: action items and timeline — we'll send SOW/pricing and security docs by 12/23, customer provides data and CIDR by 12/30, kickoff 1/6, midpoint 1/21, exec readout 1/30.
[06:16] Priya: agreed. thanks everyone.
[06:18] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. bye.
[06:22] (call ends)
